speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Communities coming together to support those in need have always existed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In the early Independence years, the social service sector was primarily made up of many small voluntary groups, each doing their best with limited resources.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To coordinate and bring together these groups, NCSS' predecessor, the Singapore Council of Social Service (SCSS) was formed in 1958.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: By 1992, rapid economic growth brought new social challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To take on a more strategic and proactive role in welfare planning and provision, SCSS was restructured to become NCSS, serving as a Statutory Board and membership body.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, social needs are more complex and cut across multiple domains such as economic and health.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Greater coordination and collaboration are needed across the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To more holistically support those they serve, social service agencies (SSAs) have expanded beyond addressing singular causes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The broader ecosystem supporting social services has also expanded.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While SSAs remain our sector's backbone, we now have more stakeholders such as social enterprises, corporates and philanthropic organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In response to these shifts, the Government and NCSS have been partnering more closely over the years to support the sector, playing distinct yet complementary roles.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) leads the development of social policies, rolls out nationwide initiatives and performs key statutory functions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, MSF has stepped up in developing, managing and co-funding a range of social services, such as family services, to raise their quality and accessibility.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS has taken a larger role as sector developer to strengthen social service delivery, build organisational and professional capabilities and develop the social service ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This has enabled NCSS to invest in building the sector's longer-term capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS has also introduced various initiatives to develop the people that deliver our services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Social Service Institute (SSI) operates as the sector's main continuing education and training centre to upskill social service professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS also supports the sector in talent attraction and retention through programmes like Sun Ray, to develop sector leadership.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In tandem with the Sector Evaluation Framework launched by NCSS in 2022, the sector now has a common language to measure the impact of services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This enables providers and funders to deliver better outcomes for service users.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Given the significant shifts in our social service landscape, MSF and NCSS reviewed how NCSS should be best positioned to continue serving the sector effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This Bill is the result of that review and reflects both NCSS' and the sector's proposals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To shape this Bill, we conducted extensive engagements with about 300 NCSS member organisations and members of the public.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Your feedback has helped us better understand the sector's needs and aspirations, and has been instrumental in shaping the current proposed amendments.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I will now share the key provisions in the Bill, which can be grouped into four key areas.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, to reflect NCSS' role as sector developer.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, to introduce a streamlined sector membership framework.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Third, to strengthen the Council, the Community Chest (ComChest) and NCSS' committees.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And fourth, to update and align the Act with those of other Statutory Boards.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The first key area relates to refreshing NCSS' objectives, functions and powers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS has responded to shifts in the landscape and expanded to become a sector developer for the social service sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS does so in three important ways which are articulated as NCSS' core objectives in the Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And third, developing the broader social service ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Clause 6 reflects this by inserting a new section 11 on objectives and functions of Council and section 12 on powers of Council.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It also gives NCSS clear functions and powers to pursue these objectives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The updated scope of NCSS' objectives and functions also clarifies its mandate to develop the wider social service sector, beyond focusing on specific stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Allow me to elaborate how NCSS' work will reflect this.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, in terms of strengthening social service delivery.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The social service sector exists to improve the lives of persons with social needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS will monitor service users' progress and make data available to the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is important so that we have a feedback mechanism for service providers, funders and philanthropic organisations to improve the outcomes for service users and increase their social impact.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS will also collect and use data to identify emerging needs and to allocate resources to services that address critical and unmet needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, in terms of building the sector's capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS will ramp up existing efforts to develop the sector's organisational and professional capabilities such as enhancing the Organisational Health Framework for Social Services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will enable service providers to identify their strengths and areas for development, so that they are better able to deliver services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS will also drive efforts to better harness volunteers and technology in the sector, enabling service providers to innovate, expand their outreach and improve services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Third, in developing the broader social service ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In the spirit of "we first", NCSS will ramp up efforts to encourage those who are able to contribute their time, talent, treasure, testimonies and ties to uplift communities in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS will pilot new ideas and technologies, and develop new partnerships with stakeholders such as social enterprises and the private sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, NCSS has embarked on a pilot with private providers to explore new ways of delivering counselling and make services more accessible.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Another example is the Social Changemaker Series, where NCSS will bring together corporates and SSAs to co-develop solutions to address needs in the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These efforts to meet the needs of service users and improve their quality of life are at the heart of NCSS' work.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The second area introduces a streamlined sector membership framework.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Membership has been central to NCSS since its early years as SCSS, when it brought different agencies in our sector together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through our engagements, many member organisations have told us that membership remains of sentimental and practical value as a platform for networking and community-building.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, NCSS has three types of membership for organisations in the sector, "Full", "Associate" and "Honorary" membership.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Organisations whose primary function is to provide a social service in Singapore or to directly support the provision of a social service in Singapore may apply to become a sector member.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: By social service, our intent is to especially cover interventions or programmes that improve the welfare of vulnerable or disadvantaged persons in Singapore, or support the emotional and psychological well-being of the local community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For instance, this would include services such as family counselling and financial assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We also took in feedback that organisations whose primary purpose is to directly support the provision of a social service are important players and should be able to apply for sector membership.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This includes professional bodies for social service professionals; organisations that mobilise resources for social service providers or service users; and organisations providing capability building to social service providers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: An organisation's eligibility for sector membership will be assessed based on a range of factors, including what it states as its objects and how it carries out its activities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With these changes, the current membership base will be rationalised and supported in their transition.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Most member organisations will experience minimal impact to their day-to-day membership experience.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is because the current criteria for Full Council members aligns with that of sector membership.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS will ease the transition for all other current Council members.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This includes honouring all existing funding support until the expiry of the support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As sector developer, NCSS will also continue to engage and support stakeholders in the wider ecosystem, beyond sector members alone.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS' priority is to deliver better outcomes for service users rather than to focus on an organisation's sector membership status, type or size.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MSF and NCSS will continue to keep open channels and engagement platforms to hear from the wider sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS' grants or other support will also be accessible to agencies whose work aligns with NCSS' priorities, even if they are not sector members.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The third key area focuses on strengthening the Council and its committees.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As NCSS' responsibilities expand, we must ensure that the Council is fit-for-purpose and understands the sector's needs, to provide effective governance and lead NCSS and the sector through the fast-changing landscape.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In line with other Statutory Boards playing a sector developer role, clause 5 provides that NCSS will be constituted and governed by its Council, headed by a Chairperson.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Clause 5 also introduces amendments to broaden representation on the Council, through a Council appointed by the Minister and widened pool of eligible candidates.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, excluding the President, half of the NCSS Board is elected by member organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We want to ensure that the sector's diversity, vibrancy and voice is reflected in the Council, and it possesses an optimal mix of skills, experience and knowledge to guide NCSS' work.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A fully-appointed Council, with nominations from sector members, will enable us to achieve this.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The practical, operational and programmatic expertise of senior management of sector members will complement the governance perspectives that other Council members can provide.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: So, putting aside the Chairperson, it will always be at least half from sector nominees.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, if there are 10 Council members appointed from sector members' nominations, the Minister will appoint at most 10 other Council members, as well as the Chairperson.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is similar to today's practice, where about half of the NCSS Board consists of individuals elected by NCSS member organisations, as earlier mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Sector members will be invited to submit one nominee each, who must be from their organisation at the point of appointment onto the Council, as a potential Council candidate.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The NCSS Chairperson, operationally assisted by a Nominations Committee comprising respected sector leaders, will submit the full list of eligible nominations to the Minister for consideration.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These changes are important as NCSS plays a critical role in the sector, as a fully funded Statutory Board with expanded objects, functions and powers as sector developer.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, the NCSS Act provides for a Board of 23 members, with a maximum term of two years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: By providing for a range in the Council size, we will have greater flexibility in determining the optimal Council size for each term, informed by the sector's needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For the incoming Council in 2026, we intend to maintain a Council size comparable to today's Board.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will allow us to balance both diversity on the Council and agility in the NCSS' decision-making.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: By setting the maximum Council term at three years, Council members will have a longer runway to contribute meaningfully to NCSS' work.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Council members may also be re-appointed, subject to the Public Service Division's (PSD's) guidelines that apply to Statutory Boards.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Along with the amendments to NCSS' committees, we will also refresh the functions of ComChest, which serves as NCSS' philanthropic and engagement arm.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The work of the social service sector directly impacts the lives of our citizens, especially those in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The social service sector has always been driven by its strong sense of purpose.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is a strong foundation for us to build upon.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As our sector faces increasingly complex social needs, our policies and institutions must continue to strengthen, support and transform the sector so that we not only meet the needs of today, but are prepared for what lies ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To build a future-ready sector, we will continue to take a strengths-based approach, be proactive to address problems upstream and adopt a whole-of-society approach.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Even with increased Government involvement, we need the continued partnership of our sector and community to support those in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS has played an instrumental role in sustaining this ethos, including by rallying the community to give their time, talent and treasure back to society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS' efforts empower stakeholders from the sector and wider community to play their part, contributing to our "we first" society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The enhancements in this Bill will further position NCSS to carry out this role.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This Bill reflects MSF and NCSS' shared commitment to building a strong and future-ready social service sector, supported by a compassionate and giving society.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: The Social and Family Development Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC) also strongly supports this Bill.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: A number of GPC Members and other colleagues from the People's Action Party (PAP) will be speaking on this Bill, contributing their views and suggestions.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: What is most noteworthy is that almost all of the Members speaking are involved in some way in the social service sector themselves.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: Some, in particular, are running, or have run, SSAs or social enterprises, for years.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: Members like Ms Denise Phua, our sector veteran or, as we would called it, one of the old OGs.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim, Ms Elysa Chen and Mr Cai Yinzhou have been in the trenches, and have a ringside view of working with and alongside NCSS.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: They will be sharing their views on what ought to be NCSS' development priorities as a sector developer.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: But more generally, all Members speaking on this Bill speak with a deep understanding of the sector and from a diversity of perspectives.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: I am thus looking forward to a very substantive and constructive debate, which can only strengthen this Bill, NCSS and ultimately, the sector.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: The Board sets the direction for NCSS and by extension, the sector.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: Ms Lee Hui Ying, Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim, Ms Elysa Chen, Mr David Hoe, Mr Cai Yinzhou, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Melvin Yong will all address this issue in their speeches.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: Ms Denise Phua, Mr David Hoe and Dr Hamid Razak will touch on this in their speeches.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: Third, the overall outcomes, impact and NCSS' measures of success going forward.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: Ms Elysa Chen, Mr David Hoe and Mr Yip Hon Weng will be speaking on this aspect.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: And finally, on the sector workforce and the heart-work that they do, every day, for every case, every client.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: Dr Wan Rizal, our labour Member of Parliament (MP), will dive deep into this topic and cover workforce development, wages and welfare.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: Mr Melvin Yong, also our labour MP, will also raise a point on sector wages, while Ms Lee Hui Ying will touch on workers' welfare and well-being in the sector.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: Beyond the substance of the debate on this Bill, let me conclude by making a point on the process that has undergirded this Bill.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: And here, I wish to commend NCSS and MSF, for undertaking a really thorough and extensive consultation process with the sector and stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: NCSS has not only listened to the sector but also responded to the feedback by actually making meaningful, substantive changes to the draft Bill.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: NCSS has demonstrated, through its consultation process for this Bill, the very spirit of collaboration and partnership with the sector that it says underpins this Bill.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: May this ethos of collaboration and partnership with the sector, in all its diversity, continue to animate NCSS, as it presses on to build a future-ready and sustainable social service sector, with the sector, to improve the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: Before I continue, I wish to declare interest in this matter, as I currently serve on the NCSS Board of Council and on the board of one of the SSAs.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: Over the past two decades, I have served in various capacities, as a volunteer, committee or board member, of several SSAs.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: From that vantage point, I have seen the sector, as Minister said, change in a fundamental way.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: The social service sector today is no longer simply a collection of charities and societies, but rather, a complex set of interdependent systems across social service provision, workforce development and cross-agency collaboration.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: As the quality of social service provision improves, coordination becomes even more essential, and this happens amidst a tight labour market, which places increasing strain on sector-wide talent pipelines.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, COVID-19 and rapid technological advances have reshaped how services are delivered and how different generations of users engage with support.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: These changes reflected, for example, in the NCSS' Quality of Life studies, have real consequences for individuals, for families and caregivers who rely on the social service system.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: First, the expanded role of NCSS as a sector developer.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: As Minister outlined earlier, NCSS today does more than convening or funding agencies.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: It identifies gaps in the system, such as the recent focus on behavioural addictions and it mobilises capacity, funding and partnerships to address them.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: It also leads sector-wide efforts in organisational development and digital transformation, so that agencies can continue to deliver services effectively and at scale.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: Initiatives, such as the Sun Ray scheme, have also strengthened workforce pipelines by bringing much needed experienced professionals from diverse backgrounds into the sector, whilst campaigns to support volunteerism and philanthropy help sustain community participation.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: These amendments recognise and formalise this expanded role.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: Second, the governance of NCSS through its Council, which is what the board is termed after proposed amendments.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: As NCSS takes on an increased role in charting sectoral priorities, building workforce pipelines and in fostering long-term partnerships, effective stewardship requires both expertise as well as continuity.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: While solutions may appear clear on the surface, the stewardship of such a complex ecosystem requires broad expertise and deep insight into the sector's many constituents and service users.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: The changes in who and how the Council is appointed, strengthens the Council so that it can work hand-in-glove with the NCSS management in setting strategic directions, exercising oversight and providing the stability needed to see these efforts through in the longer term.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: Third, the proposed size of the NCSS Council.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: This clarification notwithstanding, it is my view that the NCSS (Amendment) Bill better reflects the reality of what NCSS is responsible for – by strengthening the Council and aligning its governance with these expanded responsibilities.

speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
text: The Bill enhances NCSS' capacity to provide stable and capable stewardship of a complex and evolving social service system, and very importantly, in the interest of individuals and families that benefit from it.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Speaker, Sir, I rise to state my support for the Bill.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I declare I am an active volunteer in the disability sector for more than 25 years and I currently chair two large autism charities, both are NCSS members, and I help to supervise services from early intervention to special schools to services for adults.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In my job as Mayor of Central District Community Development Council (CDC), my team and I also partner many from the people, public and private sectors.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We work with agencies and donors to support families in need, especially those living in rental flats.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We also work with hundreds of organisations, including corporates and foundations, to raise disability awareness and dignity, through example, The Purple Parade movement and The Purple Symphony orchestra.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And NCSS is one of our key partners.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Over the years, I have seen first-hand the good work of the NCSS and its partnership-oriented approach across different generations of leadership – Ms Anita Fam, Mr Hsieh Fu Hua, Ms Ang Bee Lian, Ms Tan Li San – and many more.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: What has historically distinguished NCSS is just the policies it advanced or the funds that it administered, but its ethos as a membership-based organisation.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: NCSS had for years worked with agencies, then known as voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) and now SSAs, they work with them, rather than over them.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: NCSS recognised that effective social service delivery depends not just on structures and systems and power and hierarchy, but also on trust: trust of character and competence, professional judgement, morale and sustained relationships on the ground.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This context matters, because the Bill before us marks a clear institutional evolution.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Our social service ecosystem today is far more complex than when the principal Act was first enacted three decades ago.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The landscape is shaped by an ageing population, rising mental health needs, greater diversity amongst vulnerable groups, post-school cliff effects faced by the disabled adults, technological impact and higher expectations for accountability and outcomes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In such an environment, a stronger and better-coordinated sector is not an option, it is a necessity.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And this Bill recognises that reality, and for that, I welcome the Bill.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: However, as NCSS assumes a more formalised system-steward developer role, it becomes even more important that institutional strengthening does not dilute the partnership-driven ethos and culture that NCSS is known for.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It is from this perspective that I will highlight both the strengths of the Bill and several areas that merit careful attention.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: First, on three key positives of this Bill.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These reflect and strengthen the role of the Council as sector developer for the social service sector.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It gives statutory clarity to the Council's role as a strategic sector developer, beyond that of a convenor or a grant administrator.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It provides legitimacy for NCSS to act across boundaries and also provides a stronger governance basis for it to steward the sector responsibly and strategically.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Key positive two: stronger coordination and long-term system stewardship.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The Bill also enables NCSS to better address cross-cutting needs that spans agencies and life stages, and to reduce fragmentation within the sector.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Over time, stronger coordination can help minimise duplication, close service gaps and create clearer and more navigable service pathways, especially for individuals and families who require support from multiple touchpoints.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In this regard, the Bill can move the sector towards a more integrated and user-centered system.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The third key positive: strengthened capability development and data-informed practice.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This includes training and professional development, development of specialised skills, leadership and talent pipelines.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Taken together, these provisions support a more capable, evidence-informed sector – one that is better equipped to adapt, to learn and to respond to evolving social needs in a sustainable way, and I applaud these directions and recognise the value that they bring to a more complex and demanding social service environment.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But the very strengthening of Council's statutory role also raises important questions of balance, boundaries and execution.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: As we strengthen the system, we must not build this safety net with the chains that bind the very hands that weave it.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It is to these considerations that I now turn.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This will not bode well for the sector.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For larger SSAs, closer alignment to NCSS frameworks may result in a greater emphasis on compliance over innovation, increased risk aversion and also growing bureaucratic overheads.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I recall an instance where, sometime back, in submitting a tender for a facility for one of our charities, my team and I were required to comply with the norms and specifications that were decades old.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We were a bit stuck because non-compliance would render our tender ineligible, yet compliance would constrain our ability to innovate or pilot new models.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This illustrates how rigid requirements and compliance can sometimes discourage innovation and progress.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For smaller SSAs, stronger NCSS stewardship can bring benefits, such as access to shared services and professionalisation; and the Sun Ray Scheme, that many spoke about.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: However, uniform standards often assume an administrative scale that sometimes, smaller agencies simply do not have.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This may result in disproportionate compliance burdens, pressure to conform to standardised templates and reduced responsiveness to local community realities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The risk, therefore, is over-uniformity due to over-centralisation.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Concern number two: rising compliance and administrative burdens.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Today, funders and donors rightly expect outputs and outcomes; not to mention impact, the latest buzzword.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Some of these measures are often difficult to attribute, to isolate and to track meaningfully, especially in complex social settings.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Accountability is necessary, but it is not cost-free.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many SSAs are already operating under severe manpower constraints, high caseloads, burnout and staff turnover.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It is, therefore, important that in strengthening governance, we recognise the true cost of accountability and compliance, and avoid adding unnecessary administrative strain that will divert energy away from frontline service delivery.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This caution applies not only to administrators in the social service sector, but also across the health, ageing and special education domains.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many of Singapore's most impactful social interventions began as small, ground-up initiatives.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Pathlight School, which I co-founded, started that way.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Started by volunteers, professionals who are professionals and also parents.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We started only with 41 students, and thanks to the Ministry of Education, NCSS and SG Enable, it is now a large and popular school serving thousands.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Happee Hearts Movement, started by Dr Chen Shi Lin, started modestly and is still that way, but nimble.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So is Helping Joy – I think they are featured in the newspapers these days – started by Steven Goh, to help clear hoarding homes and thankfully, also a partner of Central Singapore CDC.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Both Dr Chen and Mr Goh are nominees for the Singaporean of the Year Award.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: If agencies, such as NCSS' expanded statutory powers, unintentionally privilege scale, maturity or compliance over proximity and trust, we risk losing such grassroots energy, and cultural and linguistic diversity, and high-touch relational approaches.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And missing contributors, such as Dr Chen and Mr Goh.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Over time, if we are not careful, agencies may default to policy-safe, standardised interventions, rather than develop innovative models to respond to emerging needs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And therefore, a healthy social service ecosystem requires not only strong institutions, but also space for diversity, for dissent and experimentation; without compromising quality and due diligence.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Concern number four: system sensing, how NCSS will identify emerging gaps.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: A stronger mandate and better data capabilities do not automatically translate into better system intelligence.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The social service landscape spans multiple vulnerable groups with overlapping, evolving and often invisible needs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many critical gaps surface first through frontline practitioners, caregivers, volunteers and even small niche organisations – long before they appear in formal data sets.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The key question, therefore, is, how will NCSS know, early and hopefully, accurately, where these urgent gaps lie, particularly when needs are localised, emergent or poorly captured by existing reporting frameworks?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And how will it know who to trust, in character and competence to work with?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, a system steward, like NCSS, must, therefore, be designed not only to coordinate, but to listen deeply, sense early and respond proportionately.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And next, on clarifying NCSS' role within the broader care ecosystem.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It is organised along different population and service domains.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For instance, those of us, as MPs, would know, seniors' services are largely coordinated by the Agency for Integrated Care under MOH; then, disability services are supported by SG Enable and MSF's Disability Office; family services and social service offices fall under MSF; and then, recently, I just heard, volunteer mobilisation, now, it is not just by NCSS, but it is also previously by National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre (NVPC) and the Prime Minister also just instructed the CDCs to look at increasing volunteers.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I think there will be overlaps, but the overlaps with existing lead agencies must be addressed in practice, especially in areas, such as needs assessment, service planning, capability development and data reporting.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Beyond relying on nominated Board members and occasional meetings of members, there should be, in NCSS, a systemic and structured platform to sense, identify, prioritise, plan, coordinate and resource the critical gaps with the other agencies, across the sector for both existing and emerging gaps.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And with that, I have three questions for the Minister, for clarification.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The first is to do with governance and innovation.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My second question is about proportionate compliance and reporting.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My third clarification question is this: it has to do with managing overlaps and identifying system gaps.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: How will all these gaps be surfaced such that they will be addressed in the sector, in a coordinated and effective and timely manner?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It strengthens coordination, builds capability and also enables a more data-informed system – one that seeks to leave fewer people behind in our society, in our country.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But at the same time, as a framework Bill, much will depend on how the Council's powers are exercised through subsequent regulations and implementation.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Its true test will, therefore, lie not in the passage of the Bill today, but in how it is applied in practice after today.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: As we strengthen NCSS and the system around it, we must also preserve the diversity, the humanity and the community-driven spirit innovation that give the sector its strength.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, in conclusion, with appreciation for the dedicated work of NCSS, Government partners, MSF and all the SSAs, and with a call for continued partnership and mutual trust, I do support the Bill.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: It is important to ensure the sector and its professionals continues to uplift lives.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: This review is timely, given how much Singapore and the world has changed.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Today, I will focus on three key points: the important role NCSS has and must continue to play; the importance of strengthening Council and committees for effective leadership; the importance of keeping ground-up social service initiatives supported; because everyone has a part and a role to play.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: (In Malay): Within our community, there are many Malay or Muslim organisations (MMOs) and all of them have channelled their efforts to build and strengthen Singapore's support ecosystem – working hand in hand with other SSAs and organizations.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Often, these organisations do not just help the Malay or Muslim community, but also the wider society who are in need.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Therefore, councils such as the NCSS are important platforms for social service practitioners to collaborate, exchange knowledge and share experiences in their efforts to improve the quality of life of Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Hence, Mr Speaker, it is also important for NCSS to ensure that council members possess comprehensive skills, understanding and representation, whether clinical or cultural.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: And as a statutory body with membership, I hope NCSS is also committed to supporting small organisations that are newly established.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: But most importantly, today's amendments should benefit Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Fundamentally, NCSS and SSAs must ensure they continue to work hand in glove.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Professor Poon earlier mentioned about "working hand-in-glove" – the same figure of speech. : Speaker, coming back to my three points.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: The important role NCSS has and must continue to play.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Over the years, NCSS role extended beyond the membership association.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I remember being elected as the President of the Singapore Muslim Women's Association (PPIS), back in 2020.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I was a COVID-19 president and the sector was tackling the pandemic, having to pivot to safer service delivery while redesigning how we engage our beneficiaries and each other.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I remembered NCSS playing a key role to support members through initiatives, such as the Beyond COVID-19 Taskforce, funding so the sector can tide through, and guidance and support to accelerate digital transformations.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: When restrictions were lifted, I remembered the NCSS Council and senior management invested time to visit member organisations and convening like-minded organisations for professional circles, so we could collaborate and learn from each other.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: One particular project I personally had a chance to work on with talented social service professionals is the NCSS' Volunteer Management Capability Development project, affectionately known as the VMCD in the sector.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: The initiative took member organisations through a comprehensive journey that helped participants develop their volunteer management policy and at the same time, strengthened resource management.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: In essence, NCSS has been driving sector development by building capabilities, enabling ecosystem partnerships and mobilising resources from people and public sectors, but more importantly, by bringing members together to identify gaps and bridge services, all toward a more inclusive and caring society.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Increasingly, social challenges are becoming more complex and interconnected, requiring multi-dimensional intervention.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Service users may find it challenging to navigate fragmented systems or interface with multiple agencies and overlapping interventions.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: As a sector developer, the outcome should also translate for service users to benefit from better coordination, resource allocation and optimisation to areas of greatest need, better lived outcomes not just now, but into the future.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Second, on a Council for diverse experts, representation and inclusion.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: The selection process for the Council should ideally reflect expertise diversity and commitment to developing the social service sector.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: This would ensure an optimal mix of skills and experience to fulfil NCSS' updated mandate.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Additionally, it is important to ensure transparency, rigour and representation in the nomination, selection and appointment process.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Needless to say, robust due diligence when assessing potential candidates is key, as is ensuring clear safeguards are in place for integrity and sector credibility and endorsement.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: NCSS must remain close to the ground especially its members, who are important resources and sounding board for the Council to remain nimble to evolving to emerging needs and even as it streamlines its membership criteria.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Having said that, NCSS should also pay close attention to ground-up initiatives in the sector, as well as support members whose membership may be affected during this transition.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: As sector developers, I hope for NCSS to continue to extend your ambit beyond your members, as has earlier been mentioned, and to support newly established SSAs to grow its impact sustainably.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: And at the core of any sector, much like Singapore, is the people.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Social service professionals should have elevated access to support for growth and development, to remain ahead of the curve and be equipped to support emerging needs of beneficiaries.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I recently spoke with a young talent, Q, who made a career switch to the sector and started his journey as a youth worker, a care staff.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: His drive saw him crossing the line to be an executive, but according to Q, his journey is an exception and not the rule.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: It reflects not only how far our social service sector has come, but also the level of stewardship now required of it.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: NCSS should continue to elevate its efforts as the drivers developing a sector that is capable, trusted and responsive to the evolving needs of our society.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: If NCSS is to take on a stronger role as a sector developer, we must be clear that sustainability cannot be measured solely by service outcomes but also by the well-being, skills development, workplace support and retention of the social and care workforce.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I will focus my remarks on what a "sector development" must mean for workers on the ground.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: A sector cannot be sustainable if its workforce is not.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: When we talk about social services, we often focus on clients and programmes, and rightly so.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: But the people delivering this work are our social and care workers, broadly defined, those on the ground doing casework, community support, caregiving, befriending, counselling, outreach and operational coordination.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: They are often under high emotional load, high caseload pressures and in a space where outcomes are not immediate and solutioning can be quite complex.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: So, if NCSS is to be a successful and well-trusted sector developer, it must go beyond ensuring service delivery and pay close attention to the workers' needs, wages, skills, welfare, employment prospects and, of course, their well-being.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It must also recognise that implementing this may increase service delivery costs and it must fulfil its duty to acquire the appropriate skills to work with the relevant Ministry to right-size funding support for the sector, so that the sector's employers can do right by their workers.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The Bill explicitly empowers NCSS to promote competencies and professional standards and to establish and maintain standards and guidelines for sector members.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I would urge the Ministry and NCSS to interpret the "sector developer" role as explicitly workforce-centred, with real accountability.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: What I hope to see are three "worker outcomes" to be developed alongside service outcomes.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Our social and care workers need structured development, entry pathways, bridging routes, advanced practice tracks, leadership development and supervision standards that protect both client and outcomes and worker well-being.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is difficult for any sector to recruit and retain talent when wage signals are unclear or comparability across sub-sectors is poor.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Today, we see differences in how wage guidelines are expressed, for example, one using basic wages while another uses gross wages.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This creates confusion for workers and makes it harder for employers to benchmark responsibly.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The social service sector is emotionally demanding and draining.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We should treat supervision quality, psychosocial safety, manageable caseloads and respect in the workplace as part of sector development, because staff burnout and turnover ultimately harm the very clients we aim to support.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Since NCSS now has a stronger sector-developer mandate and standard-setting role, can the Minister clarify how NCSS will institutionalise regular engagement with the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and the relevant unions so that worker outcomes are not incidental but are designed into the sector roadmap?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In particular, I hope NCSS will welcome a discussion with NTUC on workforce standards and job quality, because workers' issues are often raised through unions, long before their problems become visible in the system-level indicators.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: On being "direct" about wages, Sir, I think we can do both.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We can keep the principle high-level, that is, strengthen the wage competitiveness and clarity and also set a clear milestone through the harmonisation of first quarter in 2026.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We owe social and care sector workers that level of seriousness, while giving agencies and employers room to manage implementation responsibly.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The proposed framework is structured around four pillars.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I welcome this direction, because it sends a clear signal.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Being a good care provider must also mean being a good employer.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We should also encourage employers in the social services sector to access support for job redesign, training and transformation.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Where appropriate, I welcome employers to work with NTUC to explore schemes, such as the Company Training Committee grant, so that productivity improvements translate into better job quality rather than simply a higher workload.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The Bill introduces sector members and requires compliance with prescribed standards, including those for cooperation with NCSS.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This is understandable if NCSS is coordinating the sector more actively.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We must avoid where smaller organisations spend more time "servicing the system" than serving the clients.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In Malay): Sir, I support this NCSS (Amendment) Bill in principle, but its implementation must truly reflect NCSS's role as a "sector developer".

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is not about merely ensuring service delivery, but developing the social and care workforce that forms the backbone of the ecosystem with the support of our community.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The social sector does not just "help" the economy; it is a part of Singapore's economic and social infrastructure.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: When families receive timely support, workers can continue working, maintain their productivity and recover from any hardship.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In an ageing society, community care support for loved ones also becomes key to ensuring workers do not have to choose between work and family responsibilities.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In summary, to ensure better services for our people, we must first ensure that this sector offers good jobs to those entrusted to care for our community. : Mr Speaker, I hope we remember the spirit behind it.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Strengthening NCSS as a sector developer is ultimately about strengthening the whole ecosystem, the services, the organisations and the people who do the hard work behind the scenes.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: If we get this right, we will not only improve service delivery.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We will also help workers stay in the workforce because their livelihoods and families are continually supported, strengthen community care for loved ones as our population ages, protect national mental and physical well-being through upstream support, and strengthen our social safety net so that people have a real chance to bounce back and thrive.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And crucially, we will create a sector where social and care workers, central in my speech, can build meaningful careers with fair pay, progression and well-being because that is what a truly sustainable sector looks like.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: By prioritising organisations whose core business lies in the social service sector, the new Council will have the clarity and direction needed to perform its role effectively.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: First, I fully support the proposal to remove membership fees and to streamline to a single-tier membership framework.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This reduces costs in a backdrop where social service agencies are facing a double whammy of rising expenses while being hit with poorer fundraising outcomes.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In fact, a recent CNA article in December 2025, just last month, reported that some charities saw their worst fundraising season in recent years.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Given NCSS' role as sector developer, a tiered membership structure with differentiated access is no longer necessary.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: What is the percentage of members who have objectives and activities that are unrelated to the social service sector, and for this, I am truly curious as to why did they join NCSS as a member in the first place?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The Bill also proposes to shift to a fully Minister-appointed Council that will comprise of between 15 and 27 members.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This may lead to an increase of the current Council size of 23 members.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Because having too many members risks making the Council bloated and perhaps unable to come to quick decisions.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: On the other hand, if the Ministry should one day use the lower bound and appoint 15 members to the Council, what would be the considerations for this downsizing?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And how would this impact the functional performance of the Council, which traditionally has 23 members?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: However, I note that such statutory appeals are currently limited to membership decisions made by the Council.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Examples of these administrative decisions include the award and revocation of funds, which has significant impact on our SSAs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The expanded role of NCSS must be properly supported by having the right Council with a good mix of skills, knowledge and experience to drive NCSS as a sector developer.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: While I am happy to note that there will be continued sector representation in the new Council, with at least half of the Council appointed from sector members' nominations, I would like to ask the Minister what the nomination criteria would be.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We should ensure that the Council has the right subject matter expertise to drive the necessary changes to the social services sector.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Under the ComChest, fundraising is centralised and funding is then used to drive certain outcomes in the social service sector.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: How will the role of the ComChest and in particular, the functions of the staff of the ComChest, evolve with the new NCSS?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Lastly, the NCSS releases a regular salary guide for social service professionals.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is a good guide that helps organisations in the sector to benchmark salaries paid to staff without having to engage expensive consultants on their own.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: However, I understand that every edition of the salary guide causes some consternation among social service executives, some of whom have given me feedback that it is a daunting task to try to match these salary guidelines.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Many often have to sacrifice their personal time to help beneficiaries deal with issues that are complex, diverse and often multi-faceted.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As we reconstitute NCSS in its role as a sector developer, I urge the new Council to do more to build operational and professional capabilities of our social service agencies and our social service professionals to help them better cope with the ever-increasing complexity of the challenges that they face.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We must also ensure that the new Council is equipped with the right mix of skills, knowledge and experience to give success in this area.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Before I proceed, I declare my interest as the Executive Director of CampusImpact.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is a registered charity and social service agency serving children from lower-income families, and we are a member of NCSS and also a close partner of NCSS.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Over the past few decades, Singapore's social sector has made signiﬁcant strides, not just in the breadth of social provision but in the intentionality and foresight of how we plan for social needs.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In recent years, we have seen deliberate shifts across multiple sub-sectors toward more preventive, community-based and person-centred models of care.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For lower-income families, ComLink+ has moved beyond short-term ﬁnancial assistance towards long-term family coaching, bringing together Government agencies, charities and the community to support families on sustained pathways towards stability and social mobility.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In eldercare, the Age Well SG model and the development of Active Ageing Centres islandwide have embedded preventive care and social connection within our heartlands.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In the disability space, the Enabling Masterplan 2030 charts a forward-looking vision centred on inclusive employment and lifelong learning.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: These efforts are supported and enabled, in part, by NCSS, which strengthens the charities and social service agencies that undergird much of our social impact work.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Established in 1992, NCSS has progressively widened its remit to strengthen the social service ecosystem.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In 2022, NCSS also introduced the 4ST Strategic Roadmap, guiding the sector towards more collaborative, user-centric service delivery.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: At CampusImpact, NCSS support has gone beyond funding alone.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Through various capability-building and programme grants, NCSS enabled us to articulate our theory of change, develop service standards for our ﬂagship programmes, adopt digital solutions to improve our productivity and strengthen our organisational processes, while hiring talent to strengthen our management team.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Just as importantly, NCSS officers worked closely with our team to help us navigate policy parameters, reﬁne our proposals and think through implementation challenges.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This combination of ﬁnancial support and professional guidance helped a smaller agency like ours translate intent into effective delivery.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is this role, as an enabler, connector and capacity-builder, that makes NCSS more than an administrative body to the sector.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While much has been achieved, the sector faces signiﬁcant challenges ahead.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: These pressures place a high onus on NCSS' role as an anchor institution for the sector.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As this Bill seeks to formally entrench NCSS' position as a sector developer, I would like to raise several queries that relate to its long-term strategic alignment and governance.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I appreciate that sections 5(3) and 15(3) of the Bill allows employees of NCSS member organisations to sit on the Board, which would ensure that ground experience and practice wisdom is brought to discussions at the board level, ensuring greater diversity and optimising the skills, experience and capabilities of the Board.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, regarding Council appointments under sections 5 and 5F, while Ministerial appointment may strengthen strategic alignment, NCSS has historically maintained close relationships with frontline agencies and smaller charities.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What mechanisms will ensure that policy direction continues to be informed by lived realities on the ground rather than predominantly top-down considerations?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: On oversight, what are the “prescribed requirements” for sector-nominated members of the NCSS Council?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will these criteria be publicly gazetted or tabled before Parliament?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And will reasons for rejecting sector-nominated candidates or removing Council members be communicated to nominating organisations or made publicly available?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While oversight is important, NCSS plays a unique bridging role, translating sector feedback into policy reﬁnement while balancing government priorities.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What measures will ensure that NCSS retains sufficient professional independence and capacity to surface gaps in funding models, workforce sustainability and unintended policy consequences so that it remains a trusted voice for the sector rather than a purely operational arm?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While the application of the Public Sector (Governance) Act strengthens accountability, key instruments such as the NCSS Endowment Fund and the ComChest direct signiﬁcant resources across the sector.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To fully step into its role as a sector developer, it must continue to act as a central coordinator, enabling agencies to support vulnerable communities, persons with disabilities and other at-risk groups in a cohesive and complementary manner.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I appreciate Prof Kenneth Poon for recognising the close-knit network that the social service sector has grown into.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If our social service sector is much like an orchestra made of many skilled and committed players, then NCSS is not meant to play the loudest instrument.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Rather, it is the conductor, setting the tempo, ensuring harmony and allowing each organisation to contribute its strengths at the right moment.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For these reasons, Mr Speaker Sir, I rise in support of the Bill.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Social service is the quiet work of standing with people on their hardest days.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: It takes place inside homes, family service centres and conversations where people are at their most vulnerable.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: This work carries emotional weight: listening, comforting and standing with families through moments of uncertainty.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: These are the steady hands that help keep our community strong even when the challenges are not always visible.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Empowering the vulnerable members of our communities is a mission close to my heart and the hearts of my residents.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: The Bill’s proposed amendments demonstrate NCSS’ commitment to evolve its role, strengthen our social services sector and give Singaporeans the help they truly need.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I have three points of clarification, regarding first, NCSS’ mission to support sustainability of our social workers and social service officers.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Two, nomination of the board members and third, the criteria for appointing sector members.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: My first clarification relates to the sustainability of our social workers and social service officers.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: They are the foundation of our social service sector.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: If our transport workers move people, our social workers move hearts.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: We must give our social workers and social service officers the same care which they bring to the people and families they support.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Sadly, it is well known that social work has always been a very challenging career.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad that the Ministry recognises this and included in section 11 that the sustainability of the social service sector is one of the Council's statutory objectives.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: First, can the Minister share on the active steps that will be taken to meet this objective?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: What specific goals will the Council set to improve the sustainability for social workers and social service officers?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: For example, set targets to reduce caseloads, increase manpower and implement new strategies to help reduce workload for our social service officers.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Second, the Bill makes a major change in how the NCSS Board is appointed.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Having elected members, especially SSA employees on the Board is important as these elected members have a strong mandate from their peers in the social service sector to speak out on critical issues.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: It would also allow more diverse representation across different issues and groups from people who regularly interact with volunteers and beneficiaries.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: So therefore, it is extra important to uphold transparency in appointing Board members, or risk losing confidence and ownership by our social service sector in the Council.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify the rationale for removing elected members and what will be done to ensure continuity of transparency?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: These are some potential gaps which should be addressed early so that we start with the right principles to build trust.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: What criteria will guide the Minister to ensure that sector members’ nominations provide a diverse representation of the social service sector?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Could the Minister also choose to reject a nomination by the Chairman?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Will there be public disclosure of the nominations and the reasons for accepting or rejecting any nomination?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, can the Minister clarify exactly who will be eligible for NCSS Membership?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Section 15 states that NCSS would appoint or re-appoint social service agencies who apply to be sector members, defined as “  the primary function of providing or supporting the provision of social services in Singapore.” Since memberships are no longer applicable, we can take a wide definition so that more groups can benefit from the support and network the Council provides.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Would social enterprises, for example, Dignity Kitchen, informal ground-up groups or religiously affiliated social organisations be eligible to be appointed as members?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Are there any members now who would no longer be eligible for re-appointment under the new definition?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin): Mr Speaker, I support this Bill.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Social services means being quietly present with those in need during their most difficult times.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: It takes place in people's homes, at social service centres and in conversations during the most vulnerable moments.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Listening to, comforting and supporting families when they are lost and helpless inevitably involves deep emotions.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Social services are like a pair of large hands that support our community, even in places we cannot see.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: This Bill formally recognises the National Council of Social Services' (NCSS') role as a sector developer.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Through interactions with residents, I know that helping vulnerable groups in our community to become self-reliant and strong is our common vision.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: The proposed amendments in this Bill demonstrates NCSS' commitment to its developing role and strengthening the sector to better help Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I hope to have further clarifications on how we support social workers.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Social workers are the foundation of social services.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Their care drives many people forward and we also need to care for and look after social workers, in order to enable them to continue this important mission.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: We all know that social workers face enormous challenges.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
