text: Burnout, poor working conditions and manpower shortages are very real problems.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: It carries heavy emotional drain and demands emotional resilience to continue caring for others.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: With the NCSS' expanded role in developing the social service sector, I hope this enables more social organisations to be able to reach and support all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I rise in support of the NCSS (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Nevertheless, I would like to raise a few key areas for clarification, particularly on maintaining sector representation on the Council’s Board and furthering support for social enterprises.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My first clarification relates to ensuring sector representation on the Board of the Council.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The social service landscape in Singapore is highly diverse with NCSS representing over 500 SSAs that support a variety of causes such as eldercare, persons with disabilities, youths at risk, lower-income families and mental health needs.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To help the social service sector and public better understand how these new processes will be put into place, I would like to clarify the criteria for appointment to the Board.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What specific criteria will be used to select Board members and what mechanisms will be put in place to ensure a diverse and representative demographic of organisations and members on the Board?

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The ethos of the NCSS to unite communities for an inclusive and caring society is important.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We should encourage not only a diversity of sectors represented on the Board, but also diversity of individuals of different genders, age groups, ethnic backgrounds, experience and skillsets.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I strongly believe that doing so would support NCSS in its work and facilitate the balanced and holistic development of the social service sector.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second clarification relates to the relationship between NCSS and social enterprises.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Membership in NCSS is a valuable platform for the sector for networking, cross-learning and community-building opportunities.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I note that, currently, some NCSS members have registered separate social enterprises as separate entities.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In general, the operations of most social enterprises are closely intertwined with the social service sector.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The social enterprise sector strengthens social service delivery in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As the saying goes, "Give a man a fish, and you feed him for a day; but teach a man to fish and you feed him for a lifetime." Social enterprises adopt diverse business models to better align with the complex needs of different stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For instance, many provide underemployed communities with critical employment and training opportunities, such as the Social Kitchen which employs disadvantaged individuals and their caregivers; or Foreword Coffee which hires workers with special needs.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Operating social enterprise models allows them to reinvest their profits in their social missions.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This provides a more sustainable income stream for the organisation, reduces reliance on donations and provides employment for beneficiaries and expands the capacity of their social programmes.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I note that many social enterprises might be members of raiSE Singapore, which is a cross-sector collaboration between MSF, NCSS and others.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Such support could take the form of linking social enterprises with investors, connecting social enterprises with individuals in need of employment more effectively and centrally.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Additionally, could the Ministry clarify the distinction between NCSS and raiSE, in terms of the functions they will play in supporting social enterprises?

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Social enterprises would also benefit, knowing whether they can seek support and membership with NCSS in addition to with raiSE.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Notwithstanding these clarifications, I support the Bill for its decisive update to NCSS and the strengthening of the social service sector in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: The social service sector has evolved significantly over the years, as mentioned by the Minister earlier.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: It now addresses a broader and more complex range of needs, from ageing and disability to mental health, family violence and social isolation.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: In this context, I think it is timely that we update the legislative framework governing the NCSS so that it remains fit-for-purpose and well-positioned to guide the sector into its next phase of development, because when the social service sector functions well, it is our families, seniors and our vulnerable groups that will continue to do well and ultimately benefit.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I welcome the Bill's clear intent to strengthen governance, accountability and strategic clarity.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I also support the strengthened functions relating to the capability building, research, standards-setting and the ecosystem development.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: A sound and professional social service sector builds confidence through transparency, credibility, accountability and excellence, strengthening trust among stakeholders, including donors and partners who are vital to the ecosystem.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: This refinement of the sector membership framework helps sharpen the Council's engagement with organisations that are directly involved in the delivery of social services or that directly support such delivery.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: A larger Council will allow for diverse sectoral perspectives to be represented at the highest level, enabling the Council to steer the organisation effectively in an evolving landscape while also taking on the expanded functions that this Bill provides for.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: In addition, by formally engaging organisations whose primary function is to provide such social support services, the Council can strengthen partnerships with the sector while clearly maintaining lines of accountability.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: On this note, the Bill provides for clearer guidelines on the appointment and disqualification of members to the Council, among other terms, which I welcome as it enhances the professionalism and the operational efficiency of the Council.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: By addressing and correcting any perceived ambiguity, the Bill helps remove any future organisational issues.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: At the same time, I note that the Bill provides the Council with powers to prescribe standards, require cooperation and revoke sector membership in certain circumstances.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: These are understandable and necessary from a governance perspective.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: However, I would encourage the Minister and the Council to remain mindful of the importance of sector voice and autonomy.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Many SSAs operate on the frontlines, working with vulnerable individuals and families in rapidly evolving circumstances.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Ground realities often evolve faster than policy, and innovation frequently emerges from practitioners themselves.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: This is alluded to by Member Ms Dennis Phua earlier as well.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: It is therefore important that the exercise of the Council's powers continues to be accompanied by regular consultation, dialogue and co-design, so that the standards and expectations are developed collaboratively and do not unintentionally stifle innovation or discourage candid feedback from the ground.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: However, the social service sector is not uniform.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Alongside large and well-resourced agencies, there are smaller community-based organisations that serve niche and minority groups and may not have the same administrative capacity.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: In fact, personally, I have been involved and continue to be involved, in such community-based organisations that have well-intended objectives and sincere and passionate leaders but, sometimes, lack large resources and deep capabilities.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: While I understand that the Council already has existing powers under current membership, regulations to set standards and reporting requirements, I hope that these will be reviewed and operationalised under the amended framework.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I am reassured by the Ministry's commitment to engage the sector on any changes to existing requirements, so that professionalisation does not come at the expense of diversity, grassroots energy or community trust.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: The strength of this sector is also reflected in its ability to innovate and welcome new ideas, participants and members.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I also note the provisions allowing the Minister to issue directions to the Council in defined circumstances.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: The amendments relating to the ComChest are, likewise, timely.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I raise my points in the spirit of strengthening the Bill so that good governance goes hand in hand with sector vitality, innovation and inclusion.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: With these observations, I support the Bill and I look forward to its implementation, contributing meaningfully to a more resilient, responsive and compassionate social service ecosystem.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Today, I am speaking in support of the NCSS (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It aligns the law with what NCSS has been increasingly expected to do in practice: to build an effective, efficient and sustainable social service sector, and to strengthen the wider ecosystem around it, including community support and volunteerism.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Today, NCSS is seen as a sector developer.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It is expected to lead, to coordinate and to help the sector evolve.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: That said, as we strengthen the NCSS' mandate, it is important to carefully think about how these powers are exercised in practice.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: And for this, I would like to raise five points for consideration.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: First, there is a risk of over-centralisation and perceived distance from the ground.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Stronger coordination is the intent of the Bill, and rightly so.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It is important to note that any system-steward model, where the role is not only just merely an operator, regulator or content owner, but as a caretaker of the wider ecosystem, it carries a trade-off.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: However, one concern on the ground with NCSS taking on this role that we are here is, will it create more rules and frameworks that actually discourage experimentation?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: If we over-standardise, we may unintentionally dampen the local innovation that specialises in serving specific communities.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: In my conversation with many agencies, many often innovate because they know what works for the community that they interact with.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Many try new outreach methods, new approaches, culturally sensitive approaches or partnerships with schools and employers.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: But if standards become too rigid, then the "cost of trying something new" rises.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Staff may worry that a pilot will fail an audit requirement, fall outside prescribed service boundaries or create additional reporting burden.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: All these can create a risk-averse culture where agencies stick to safe, familiar programmes, even when emerging needs require new approaches.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: In this regard, social needs are not uniform.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: What works for seniors living alone might not work for youths-at-risk.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: What works for families living in a rental block may not work for persons with disabilities navigating employment.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Hence, we should strive to continue supporting innovative and tailored approaches as we journey towards strengthened sector coordination with this Bill.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: One possible way forward is a "standards-plus-sandbox" approach over clear baseline for safety and governance, paired with structured space for innovation and differentiated models.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: This allows for consistency without crowding out creativity on the ground.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: My second point, like many have mentioned, is Council composition and sector nominations.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It also allows the Chairperson to exclude nominees who do not meet prescribed requirements.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Also, when appointing the members of this Council, the Minister must consider whether the members of the Council will collectively possess appropriate knowledge, skills and experience for the Council to perform its functions effectively.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Against this backdrop, I was asked what is considered "appropriate knowledge, skills and experiences".

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: From my viewpoint, it should not be narrowly read as titles or credentials.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It should include practical exposure to service users' journeys; for instance, having prior experience on seeing how a resident moves from first contact to assessment, to referral, to ongoing support.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: This enables an understanding of where friction occurs, where people fall through the cracks and what dignity in service actually looks like.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: They are practical lenses that help a Council to anticipate unintended consequences, blind spots in standards and design policies that citizens can actually live with.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: We must also avoid the possibility of a perception risk where nomination pipelines are dominated by larger agencies with more administrative capacity and wider networks.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: While I do not think every detail needs to be hard-coded into primary legislation, I think a clearer competency framework would strengthen confidence in how the Council is constituted.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Put simply, the Council should collectively cover a balanced mix of core skill sets.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: For example: service delivery and practice insight; skills in governance, risk, audit, finance, accountability; sector capabilities and an eye on quality improvement.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: At the same time, beyond skill sets, the Council should be mindful of representation across sectors, including diversity across sub-sectors that ensuring smaller and specialised SSAs have a meaningful voice.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: At the heart of it, Mr Speaker, Sir, it is not about excluding anyone; we know everyone can bring something to the table, but what is also equally important is what exactly does this table needs so that we can be more effective in the work that we do.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Third, we should also avoid unintentional compliance burdens on smaller agencies, as mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: This direction is sound since standards protect service users.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: But there is also a real risk if compliance becomes too heavy or too uniform.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: This, in my view, is a proxy indicator for broader compliance risks.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: We should avoid a situation where: reporting becomes a hidden tax on smaller SSAs; agencies with weaker back-office capacity fall behind; compliance becomes a proxy for quality, but actually they are not always the same.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: In my view, I think a proportionate, tiered approach to standards, supported by templates, shared tools, transitional support, would help to ensure that raising the floor does not inadvertently shrink the sector.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Smaller community-based agencies should not be weighed down by the same administrative burdens as large, system-critical providers, while agencies serving more vulnerable populations should rightly face with higher safeguards.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Paired with shared tools, templates and transitional support, such an approach will allow us to protect service users without unintentionally squeezing out innovation or capacity on the ground.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: My fourth point on procedural fairness must be clear and accessible.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: These safeguards are important, but they must be usable in practice.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: In the guidance, it would be helpful to ensure that: there are clear written reasons for refusal; there are reasonable timelines and plain-language appeal templates; accessibility support for smaller agencies with limited administrative capacity is made available and accessible; and a predictable and transparent processes that are laid out so that this regime, this process is experienced as a fair one rather than an arbitrary one.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The Bill anchors NCSS' objectives clearly: effectiveness, efficiency, sustainability, stronger delivery, capability and ecosystem development.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: But citizens are also looking for measurable signals.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: And social services are, by definition, a "go-together" endeavour.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: If we pair these reforms with fair processes, proportionate standards, transparent governance and real sector voice, this Bill can help to build a social service system that is both stronger and more trusted.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: With these points, Mr Speaker, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They judge our social service system by its real-world impact: does help arrive on time?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, the composition of the Council determines the sector's perspective.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Who sits at the table potentially decides what issues are prioritised and more importantly, what blind spots remain.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Families in rental flats often rely on small agencies and volunteers who see early warning signs that larger systems miss.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Council should reflect the realities of those who work closest to danger.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While this provides representation, it may not automatically secure independence or the necessary frontline perspective.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Furthermore, under clause 5(3), the Chairperson may exclude nominees who do not meet "prescribed requirements".

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If these are not transparent, we risk screening out plain-speaking, ground-level voices.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must also guard against over-selecting representatives from organisations whose funding incentives align them towards administrative stability rather than candour.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Council needs "risk signal specialists" whose duty is to identify blind spots, not simply reinforce consensus.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While I understand the need for confidentiality in state security, social services deal with safety.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If a Ministerial direction effectively changes escalation thresholds for child abuse or elder neglect, and that direction is sealed, how can this House scrutinise whether those thresholds are safe?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We cannot provide a counterbalance to what we cannot see.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I ask if Parliament could at least receive an anonymised annual briefing on such directions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: After reviewing past cases involving systemic lapses and delayed escalation, this can be concerning.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If clause 11(2)(b) empowers NCSS to coordinate the sector, authority must be paired with responsibility.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Should NCSS not have a statutory responsibility to lead serious case reviews and publish anonymised lessons?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While I support protecting social workers from frivolous liability and recognise the difficult judgement calls they face on the ground, "good faith" must not become a shield for repeated oversight.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must ensure this immunity does not inadvertently reduce the incentives for rigorous self-critique.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: When no one is legally responsible, everyone becomes morally invisible.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: When every agency can point to a process that was technically and legally followed, cases can still fall through the cracks.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, I am concerned that the broad powers to appoint or remove sector members may unintentionally make agencies more cautious about escalation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Many agencies serving my residents are small and nimble.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could a passionate agency that challenges policy gaps be misinterpreted as acting against "public interest"?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We need clarity on how public interest is distinguished from administrative convenience.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Furthermore, section 15(4) requires "cooperation with the Council" as a condition of membership.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must ensure that "cooperation" is not misread as "compliance".

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: True cooperation includes the duty to raise concerns, notify relevant authorities and comply with the law by lodging police reports where necessary.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Sometimes, the most constructive partnership is demonstrated when an agency says, "You are wrong, and this child is in danger." This Bill must protect such engagement as a vital form of cooperation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: On recourse: under section 16, appeals regarding membership go back to the Minister.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What prevents this from becoming a circular loop without independent review?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If an agency is removed for being too vocal about a systemic failure, appealing to the Ministry that oversees that system provides little reassurance.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We should ensure long-serving members and volunteers feel recognised, not dismissed so they remain empowered to speak up.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This Bill must strengthen the courage of the sector, not the caution.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, Sir, the new "sector developer" powers under section 11 must translate into real-world outcomes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Residents measure success simply: when we call for help, does someone actually come?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I have four questions on how this will be operationalised.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Specifically, will this include mechanisms to detect risk across systems and agencies early?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Past tragedies have shown that failures often arise not from the absence of services but from fragmented information and lack of shared visibility.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We need a system that links data so that when, say, a child goes missing in one domain, the alarm rings in all.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How do we prevent over-standardisation from suppressing local innovation?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Often, ground-up charities spot risks first because they are not following a rigid, top-down template.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Standardisation must raise the floor without lowering the ceiling of innovation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A rental block in Yio Chu Kang faces different pressures from, say, a Build-To-Order (BTO) in Punggol.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Should NCSS not publish region-level indicators of responsiveness, instead of only national averages?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A national average of "90% satisfaction" is of no comfort to a neighbourhood where the response time is three weeks.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: That matters, because residents do not experience systems in theory.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They ask simple questions: does help arrive on time?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Having listened carefully to the various speeches today, there is a clear conversion in our PAP MPs' views.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Accountability and data use must be match by transparency, proportionality and trust.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Coordination must strengthen, not weaken, responsiveness to frontline realities, small agencies and emerging needs.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is in this collective spirit that the clarifications raised today should be considered.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These shared concerns bring us back to why this Bill matters and why its design choices matter.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We should not pass this legislation in a vacuum.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We pass it with the memory of every case where the system hesitated, fragmented or deferred when it needed to act.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The names change, but the lessons do not.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: When a warning light flickers, the system must sharpen, not soften.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It must protect, not disappear into administrative cracks.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If we shape NCSS into a body that welcomes frank voices, values ground insight, supports escalation and learns from failure, this Bill will do more than restructure a Council.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It will strengthen the safety net for every child, every senior, every caregiver and every vulnerable person in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I hear their aspirations, their caution and I take them in good spirit.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I am heartened by the care shown for the social service sector and the endorsement of NCSS' work.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Members have expressed broad support for NCSS' role as a sector developer, the value of sector membership and the need for a diverse and representative Council.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I will now address the questions and clarifications that Members have raised.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Lee Hui Ying, Mr Cai Yinzhou, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr David Hoe asked for clarifications on sector membership.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NCSS will look at each application and assess the organisation's objectives and activities against these criteria.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, about 400 of them, since the criteria for Full Council membership align with those of sector membership.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Current Associate Council members who meet the criteria are welcome to apply for sector membership.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But there may be some organisations, such as those whose primary functions do not relate to social services within Singapore, which would not qualify for sector membership.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Such organisations are a subset of all Associate Council Members, and joined NCSS at a time when the membership criteria was much broader.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NCSS will ease this transition, including honouring any existing support until its expiry.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On social enterprises, the Singapore Centre for Social Enterprise (raiSE), established by MSF, serves as the dedicated membership body to provide them tailored support and resources.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Moving forward, if a social enterprise also wishes to be an NCSS sector member, its application will be assessed, in consultation with raiSE, on a case-by-case basis, depending on its objectives and activities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Nevertheless, as a sector developer, NCSS will work with partners in the ecosystem regardless of their sector membership status to find solutions to our social challenges.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Indeed, over the years, NCSS has been working closely with raiSE – itself a current NCSS member organisation – to build stronger enterprise capabilities in the sector for financial sustainability and partnerships between SSAs and social enterprises to better serve users.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Yip, Mr Hoe and Dr Hamid Razak asked about the rejection and revocation of sector membership and appeals to the Minister for such decisions, emphasising the importance of transparency and independence of such processes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In particular, Mr Yip asked if agencies that challenge policy gaps could be misinterpreted as acting against the public interest.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I assure Members that we want to continue to have constructive conversations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In fact, we welcome diverse views and suggestions, including surfacing challenges and gaps in existing policies and programmes, that can help us strengthen the ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The aim of these powers is to ensure that organisations meet the criteria for sector membership and to safeguard the diverse yet cohesive, responsible and respectful social service sector that we have built over the years.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is also the thinking behind the clause requiring that sector members' aims, objects and activities do not go against public interest, public order or national harmony.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The appeal mechanism is also precisely in place as a check and balance for NCSS' sector membership decisions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Sector membership applications will first be assessed by the Council.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Appeals will only go to the Minister if an applicant disputes a decision that the Council stands by.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We agree with Mr Hoe on the importance of transparency and the appeal processes and timelines will be clearly communicated.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I will now move on to the Council-related comments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Elysa Chen, Mr Hoe, Ms Lee and Mr Yip asked how we can ensure diverse representation under a fully-Minister appointed Council.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To further expand the range of perspectives, we have also proposed amendments to allow employees of sector members to be appointed onto the Council, since their expertise and experience will provide important ground perspectives, as Ms Lee also observed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Based on our past experience with the NCSS Board, the results of elections are dependent on who chooses to run at the annual general meeting (AGM), how well-known the candidates are amongst those voting and sometimes, how influential the nominating organisation is.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The shift to a fully appointed Council allows for the composition of the Council to be considered as a whole, so that it better represents the sector and has the necessary mix of skills and perspectives.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This brings me to the specific criteria and process for Council appointments, which Ms Chen, Mr Yip, Mr Cai, Ms Lee, Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim, Mr Yong and Mr Hoe asked about.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As Mr Hoe rightly pointed out, it is not desirable for every detail and criterion to be hardcoded in primary legislation, and trying to do so may introduce unnecessary rigidity that will not be helpful to NCSS functioning effectively, particularly as needs change in the future.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are working out the specific implementation details and will share more with sector members in due course.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As Prof Poon pointed out, NCSS needs broad expertise and deep sector insight to effectively steward the sector.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Broadly, we will consider whether individuals have relevant experience in senior leadership, governance or social service.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We would also look out for individuals with specific skillsets, like law, finance or technology.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Beyond professional credentials, experience on the ground is also important.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Process-wise, the Chairperson will submit all nominations to the Minister, except for those which do not meet requirements prescribed by Regulations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These prescribed requirements cover procedural matters, such as each sector member nominating only one individual from their organisation, which would include their board members, and fully completing application forms.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As earlier shared, a Nominations Committee will be established to assist with the nominations process.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To Ms Hazlina's points, the committee will comprise individuals with diverse experience, expertise and high standing in the sector.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will share details of the composition of the committee in due course.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Yong and Prof Poon asked about the rationale behind providing for a range in the Council size, with an increased maximum size of 27, and how the exact size will be determined in practice.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Chen and Ms Lee asked if the reasons for rejecting nominations or removing Council members would be communicated.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Sector members will be notified of the outcome of their nominations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If there are prescribed requirements that the nominees do not meet, we may inform the sector member accordingly.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the removal of Council members, even though the Bill provides that the Minister is not obliged to provide reasons, where appropriate, we will engage the relevant Council member in the exceptional circumstances where the Minister has to exercise the power.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Yip asked about the transition for current NCSS Board and committee members.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Yip may be assured that MSF and NCSS values the work of all who serve on NCSS' committees and Board and recognises them through various platforms.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I would also like to highlight that at the end of the day, Council appointments are not the only avenue for sector voices to be heard.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As sector developer, NCSS will continue to closely engage the sector, gather insights from the ground, and partner with the Government to strengthen outcomes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the last few years, NCSS has been organising leadership visits between MSF's and NCSS' management and SSAs, small group engagements with Board leaders, on top of large-scale engagements, workshops and clinics that are open to all NCSS member organisations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MSF and NCSS value the views, insights and work of our ecosystem players, and will continue listening to and co-creating with the sector.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Like many Members stressed in their speeches, the key is to have processes that build trust.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There is no single perfect system or process, but it will be in the conduct of each nomination and appointment, and in the everyday engagements and partnerships that NCSS forms with stakeholders in social services, that we strengthen the trust that we have built over the years.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Lastly, I want to address the most important issue, which is the impact of the changes on the users of social services, the sector and society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As Ms Denise Phua noted, this Bill will indeed strengthen NCSS' role, as sector developer, to coordinate services to provide more effective and efficient support to those in need, and raise the sector's organisational and digital capabilities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As social issues have become increasingly cross-cutting, NCSS will work closely with relevant Government agencies across different domains and leverage inter-agency platforms and mechanisms to identify and meet service users' needs holistically and in a coordinated manner.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: A few Members also asked about the implications of the Bill for innovation in the sector.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Phua, Ms Chen, Dr Hamid, Dr Wan Rizal, Mr Hoe and Mr Yip expressed concerns about the potential impact of NCSS setting standards on sector members, especially smaller ones, as well as of the Ministerial power to issue directions to NCSS.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is in NCSS' DNA to work with the sector to incubate ideas to meet emerging needs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NCSS also supports innovation in the sector, for example, through the National Design Challenge, a platform where anyone can step forward to design solutions for social issues.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The need to meet standards and obligations set by NCSS is not new to current Council Members.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Broadly similar obligations already exist in subsidiary legislation under the NCSS Act today and are intended to protect service users, for accountability and to uplift the sector.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, today, Full Council Members must submit copies of their annual report, audited accounts and balance sheet to NCSS yearly.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is important, given that many of these organisations, who will become sector members after the amendments, receive donations and public funds and must steward these resources appropriately.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NCSS is always mindful of the compliance load on member organisations, particularly small ones, when new standards and obligations are introduced.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We thank Mr Hoe, Ms Phua and Dr Hamid for their suggestions to take a proportionate approach and provide sufficient time and capacity-building support for sector members to meet any standards imposed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NCSS will support and engage sector members when implementing any new standards and do so in a practical manner, including providing relevant resources and training, as it has been doing.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In response to Mr Yong's query on the functions and governance of ComChest, the amendments do not change the fundraising function of ComChest.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The updated governance provisions apply to the conduct and management of ComChest, rather than grant recipients.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Besides impact on organisations, Ms Lee, Dr Rizal and Ms Hazlina asked about the impact on professionals.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is indeed both MSF's and NCSS' intent to support our social service professionals and we have been doing so.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In recent years, NCSS has embarked on several initiatives to address sector manpower needs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This includes funding SSAs through the Transformation Sustainability Scheme to enhance their people management practices, redesigning jobs and augmenting manpower with volunteers and technology.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We share Dr Rizal's views that worker well-being is important and have rolled out various initiatives to support our sector professionals.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: More details will be shared later this year.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ensuring good jobs in the sector will continue to be part of NCSS' work as sector developer and we will work with all stakeholders, including sector members, unions and MOH to ensure there are quality jobs and clear salary guidelines in the sector.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the Ministerial power to issue directions, this is part of the governance framework for all Statutory Boards and there is already a broadly similar power under the NCSS Act today.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is not intended to interfere with NCSS' exercise of its functions or limit NCSS from representing feedback from the sector.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We value the critical function that NCSS plays in reflecting the sector's voice, to ensure that our policies are grounded in operational needs and realities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Yong asked about the channels to provide feedback on NCSS's administrative decisions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Both MSF and NCSS have open channels for organisations to provide feedback and we are committed to ensure that our policies and programmes are effective in meeting their outcomes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I also ask for Members' understanding that I will not be able to address some of Members' other queries and comments that go beyond the remit of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This Bill has been several years in the making.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NCSS first formally engaged the sector on the proposed amendments at its AGM in July 2024.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Since then, there have been many further engagement sessions, which have helped shape the Bill before us today.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Many Members, including Ms Phua, Dr Hamid and Ms Chen, highlighted the importance of preserving the sector's voice and of continuing to engage the sector and ensure coordinated action across stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To echo Mr Xie Yao Quan's observation, this is indeed what MSF and NCSS have been doing, including through the consultation process for this Bill and will continue to do.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This Bill strengthens NCSS' ability to act as the bridge for sector feedback to be translated into policy.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: With this Bill, NCSS will be well positioned to lead the sector to achieve better outcomes and improve the quality of life of users of our social services.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have been in the Chamber for over four hours, so I propose to take a break now.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will suspend the Sitting and will assume the Chair at 4.30 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 4.12 pm until 4.30 pm.
